title: Quiescent current (excl. load current) at no load and full load
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's "Iq (excl. load current)" row (< 30uA at no load and full load) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch), using the row's own two named load points. That row is the one row DR-006 left open when issue #1 ratified the rest of the table: its number is set by spec/decision-records/DR-009-iq-budget.md, whose status is 'proposed' -- DR-009 does not ratify itself, and ratifies only when the pull request it ships in merges (the same path DR-006 took). The bound below cites DR-009's number verbatim, not an invented final limit, and needs re-verification if that record changes before it merges. Each corner runs two cold-start, settled transients (0mA then 50mA, via the deck's own 'alter' on the load current source, mirroring sim/loop-gain's multi-point convention from #25): Iq is defined, per design/README.md's own "Iq = total VIN current minus load current" convention, as -i(vvin) at no load (no subtraction needed) and as -i(vvin) minus the deck's own known 50mA load constant at full load, each averaged over its point's settled 199ms-200ms tail. Initial-condition contract (issue #171, converted by #173): each point is 'tran 10u 200m uic' with the testbench's VEN stepping high at 101us -- NOT the bare unconstrained two-'.op' chain this bench used through record 20260910-034648-6c0436d, the worst case of the unconstrained-'.op' defect #164 characterized: all 45 of that record's corners carried a solver diagnostic ('singular matrix' or 'out of range for ^'), which sim/bin/corner-run.py's #171 gate now forces to FAIL outright. This bench reuses load-regulation's own measured 199ms-200ms settling window (#172) rather than re-deriving it, because both benches share the same 1uF COUT / 10mOhm RESR output network and the same iload 'alter' shape -- the settling time is a property of that shared network. Known risk, not a testbench defect -- and confirmed during this testbench's own bring-up, not just cited from elsewhere: design/README.md's dated 2026-08-25 root-cause section (issue #60, mechanism 1; tracked by #69) documents a thermal-shutdown false-trip at the ff/sf process corners at 125C, independent of load current; a direct check at ff/125C/3.63V (screening, not part of this record) confirms TS_CMP=0.39V (tripped; untripped is approximately VIN) and vout collapsed to -19.2V at full load (0.14V at no load) at that exact corner, yet -i(vvin) itself still reads a plausible-looking, in-budget microamp figure there rather than an obviously non-physical one -- unlike line-regulation/load-regulation, where the same false-trip produces an unmistakably out-of-range number. Regulation gate (issue #133, folded into #173): vout_no_load_v/vout_full_load_v are now bounded to the ratified Output row's 1.764-1.836V window, and iq_no_load_ua/iq_full_load_ua now carry a 'min: 0' floor, rather than being reported unbounded -- a corner whose operating point is not really regulating (e.g. the thermal-shutdown false-trip above, or a non-physical negative supply current) now fails outright instead of relying on a reader to notice a plausible-looking, in-budget Iq figure next to an out-of-window vout. This mirrors sim/enable-shutdown/experiment.json's existing vout_pre_disable_v regulation-gate pattern (bounded to the same 1.764-1.836V window) rather than inventing a new mechanism. #133's own two named non-physical corners (ss_-40c_3.30v no-load; ff_-40c_2.97v full-load) were measured against the pre-#173 unconstrained-'.op' chain; this record re-measures both under the seeded chain, since seeding can change which corners are non-regulating.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: * Each point is a COLD-START, SETTLED transient, not a bare
* at its natural cold value with EN low (the testbench's VEN steps high
* at 101us), so the block powers up through its own soft-start ramp and
* no operating-point solve happens at all. Both the vout reading and the
* VIN supply current are averaged over the settled 199ms-200ms tail --
* Iq needs the same settled window vout does, since any residual COUT

meas tran vout_no_load avg v(vout) from=199m to=200m
meas tran iq_no_load_raw avg i(vvin) from=199m to=200m
meas tran vout_full_load avg v(vout) from=199m to=200m
meas tran iq_full_load_raw avg i(vvin) from=199m to=200m

measurements.name: iq_no_load_ua
measurements.note: Total VIN supply current (I_LOAD=0, so no subtraction needed), averaged over the no-load point's settled 199ms-200ms tail (issue #173; the `tranN.` plot prefixes replace the pre-#173 `opN.` ones). Bound set by DR-009 ('proposed', not yet ratified): spec/target-spec.md "Iq (excl. load current)" row, < 30uA at no load. `min: 0` (issue #133, folded into #173): a genuinely regulating corner cannot draw negative supply current, so a negative reading is itself proof of a non-physical operating point and must fail rather than pass a max-only bound vacuously -- this bench's prior record scored exactly that at ss_-40c_3.30v (-3348.61uA).

measurements.name: iq_full_load_ua
measurements.note: Total VIN supply current minus the deck's own known 50mA load constant, averaged over the full-load point's settled 199ms-200ms tail (issue #173; the `tranN.` plot prefixes replace the pre-#173 `opN.` ones). Bound set by DR-009 ('proposed', not yet ratified): spec/target-spec.md "Iq (excl. load current)" row, < 30uA at full load. `min: 0` (issue #133, folded into #173): same non-physical-negative-current floor as iq_no_load_ua -- this bench's prior record scored exactly that at ff_-40c_2.97v (-3357.86uA).

measurements.name: vout_no_load_v
measurements.note: Regulation gate (issue #133, folded into #173): bounded to the ratified Output row's +-2% window (1.764-1.836V, spec/target-spec.md), mirroring sim/enable-shutdown/experiment.json's vout_pre_disable_v pattern, so a corner that is not really regulating (e.g. the thermal-shutdown false-trip design/README.md documents) fails outright instead of merely being reported for a reader to notice next to a plausible-looking, in-budget Iq figure -- see this experiment's own claim. Previously reported unbounded (min/max both null).

measurements.name: vout_full_load_v
measurements.note: Same regulation gate as vout_no_load_v (issue #133, folded into #173), at the full-load (50mA) point. Previously reported unbounded (min/max both null).
